title: How Wooden Products Are Made
description: From rough timber to a hand-finished heirloom — inside our wood workshop.
body: Every wooden piece begins with carefully selected, sustainably sourced timber. Our artisans read the grain, rough-cut the blank, then shape it with chisels and gouges before hours of sanding and hand-oiling. The result is a piece that feels alive in the hand and only grows more beautiful with use.
author: The Workshop

sections.heading: 1. Selecting the Timber
sections.text: We hand-pick sustainably sourced hardwood logs, inspecting each one for grain direction, moisture and natural character. Only the best blanks make it to the bench. [Replace this text and the image with your own workshop photos and description.]

sections.heading: 2. Cutting & Shaping
sections.text: The rough blank is cut to size and shaped with chisels, gouges and the lathe. Our artisans follow the natural grain so every curve feels intentional. [Replace this placeholder text and image later.]

sections.heading: 3. Sanding & Finishing
sections.text: Hours of progressive sanding bring the surface to a silky finish, followed by hand-rubbed food-safe oil that deepens the color and protects the wood. [Add your real finishing process and images here.]

title: How Resin Products Are Made
description: Pouring oceans — the patient art of layered epoxy resin.
body: Resin art is equal parts chemistry and intuition. We mix pigments by hand, pour in careful layers, and let each cure before adding the next. Gold leaf and mica catch the light to create depth that looks like a frozen wave.
author: Studio Team

sections.heading: 1. Mixing the Resin
sections.text: We measure epoxy resin and hardener precisely, then blend by hand to a crystal-clear base ready for color. [Replace this text and image with your own process photos.]

sections.heading: 2. Adding Pigments & Color
sections.text: Mica powders, pigments and gold leaf are added layer by layer to build depth and movement, like a frozen wave. [Add your real coloring details and images here.]

sections.heading: 3. Pouring & Curing
sections.text: Each layer is poured carefully and left to cure fully before the next, a slow process that prevents bubbles and cracks. [Swap this placeholder later.]

sections.heading: 4. Sanding & Polishing
sections.text: Once cured, the piece is sanded smooth and polished to a glass-like shine before final inspection. [Replace with your own finishing snapshots.]

title: How Leather Products Are Made
description: Full-grain leather, saddle-stitched the traditional way.
body: We start with vegetable-tanned full-grain hides, cut by hand and burnished at every edge. Each stitch is pulled tight by hand so it never unravels — the mark of leather goods built to last a lifetime.
author: Leather Atelier

title: How Chef Knives Are Made
description: Forged, ground and balanced — the making of a chef's knife.
body: Our knives are forged for hardness and edge retention, then hand-ground to a razor finish. Handles are shaped from stabilized hardwood and fitted for perfect balance, so the blade becomes an extension of your hand.
author: Blade Smith

title: Quality Inspection
description: Why every single piece is checked by a human, twice.
body: Before anything ships, it passes a two-stage inspection: structural integrity and finish quality. If it isn't good enough to keep ourselves, it doesn't leave the workshop.
